indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.2.1 Demonstrate understanding of the life cycle of plants
indicator.objective: Observe, identify and give functions of the parts of a plant

skills.description: Name the main parts of a plant: root, stem, leaf, flower.
State the function of the root (absorbs water and mineral salts; holds the plant in the soil).
State the function of the stem (supports the plant; carries water and food between root and leaves).
State the function of the leaf (makes food for the plant using sunlight).
State the function of the flower (produces seeds/fruits; helps in reproduction).
Link a part's position on the plant to its function (e.g. roots are underground because they absorb water from soil).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Roots only hold the plant; they do not take in water.
Leaves only make the plant look green.
The stem is only for beauty.
Flowers are only for decoration; they have no job.
All parts of a plant do the same work.
Roots are always the biggest part of the plant.

questions.stem: Which part of a plant is usually found under the ground?
options: Leaf
Flower
Root
Stem
hints: Which part holds the plant in the soil?
It grows downwards into the ground.
questions.explanation: The root is usually found under the ground. It holds the plant in place and takes in water from the soil.
questions.misconception: All parts of a plant grow above the ground.

questions.stem: Which part of a plant is usually green and flat?
options: Root
Leaf
Flower
Stem
hints: Which part catches sunlight?
It grows out from the stem.
questions.explanation: The leaf is usually green and flat. It catches sunlight to make food for the plant.
questions.misconception: Leaves only make the plant look green.

questions.stem: Which part of a plant is often colourful and produces seeds?
options: Root
Stem
Leaf
Flower
hints: Which part attracts insects?
It produces fruits and seeds.
questions.explanation: The flower is often colourful and produces seeds and fruits. It helps the plant reproduce.
questions.misconception: Flowers are only for decoration.

questions.stem: What is the main job of the root?
options: To make food for the plant
To absorb water from the soil
To produce flowers
To catch sunlight
hints: Roots are under the ground.
They take in water from the soil.
questions.explanation: The main job of the root is to absorb water and mineral salts from the soil. It also holds the plant in place.
questions.misconception: Roots only hold the plant; they do not take in water.

questions.stem: What is the main job of the leaf?
options: To hold the plant in the soil
To absorb water from the soil
To make food for the plant using sunlight
To carry water to the roots
hints: Leaves are green.
Green leaves use sunlight to make food.
questions.explanation: The leaf makes food for the plant using sunlight. The green colour in leaves helps trap sunlight.
questions.misconception: Leaves only make the plant look green.

questions.stem: What is the main job of the stem?
options: To support the plant and carry water between roots and leaves
To absorb water from the soil
To produce seeds
To make food for the plant
hints: The stem stands upright.
It connects the roots to the leaves.
questions.explanation: The stem supports the plant and carries water and food between the roots and the leaves.
questions.misconception: The stem is only for beauty.

questions.stem: What is the main job of the flower?
options: To absorb water from the soil
To carry water to the leaves
To make food from sunlight
To produce seeds and fruits for reproduction
hints: Flowers produce something that can grow into new plants.
Seeds are found in fruits.
questions.explanation: The flower produces seeds and fruits. This helps the plant to reproduce.
questions.misconception: Flowers are only for decoration.

questions.stem: A farmer pulls a plant from the ground and finds many thin roots spread out in the soil. What are these roots doing?
options: They are making food for the plant
They are absorbing water and holding the plant in the soil
They are producing flowers
They are catching sunlight
hints: Roots are in the soil.
They take in water and hold the plant.
questions.explanation: The roots spread out in the soil to absorb water and minerals and to hold the plant firmly in the ground.
questions.misconception: Roots only hold the plant; they do not take in water.

questions.stem: Why is the root found under the ground?
options: So that it can catch sunlight
So that it can absorb water from the soil and hold the plant in place
So that it can produce flowers
So that it can carry food to the leaves
hints: Water is in the soil.
The root holds the plant down.
questions.explanation: The root is under the ground so it can absorb water from the soil and hold the plant firmly in place.
questions.misconception: Roots are above the ground.

questions.stem: Name two parts of a plant.
hints: Think of what you see above and below the ground.
One part is green and flat; another is under the soil.
questions.explanation: The main parts of a plant are the root, stem, leaf and flower.
questions.misconception: Plants only have leaves.

questions.stem: What does the stem do for the plant?
answer: it supports the plant and carries water and food
it holds the plant upright and carries water between the roots and the leaves
hints: The stem stands upright.
It connects the root to the leaf.
questions.explanation: The stem supports the plant and carries water and food between the roots and the leaves.
questions.misconception: The stem is only for beauty.

questions.stem: Which TWO jobs does the root do for the plant?
options: Makes food and produces flowers
Absorbs water and holds the plant in the soil
Catches sunlight and carries water to leaves
Produces seeds and absorbs sunlight
hints: The root is under the ground.
It does two main things.
questions.explanation: The root absorbs water from the soil and holds the plant firmly in place.
questions.misconception: Roots only hold the plant; they do not take in water.

questions.stem: Why are leaves important to a plant?
answer: they make food for the plant using sunlight
leaves make food for the plant
they use sunlight to make food
hints: Leaves are green.
Green leaves use sunlight.
questions.explanation: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight. Without leaves, the plant cannot make its own food.
questions.misconception: Leaves only make the plant look green.

questions.stem: Why are most leaves found at the top of the plant, spread out?
options: So that they can catch as much sunlight as possible
So that they can absorb water from the soil
So that they can hold the plant in the soil
So that they can produce seeds
hints: Where does sunlight come from?
Leaves need sunlight to make food.
questions.explanation: Leaves are spread out at the top of the plant to catch as much sunlight as possible for making food.
questions.misconception: Leaves are only for decoration.

questions.stem: What is the main function of a flower?
answer: it produces seeds and fruits for the plant to reproduce
hints: Flowers produce something that grows into new plants.
Seeds are found in fruits.
questions.explanation: The flower produces seeds and fruits. This helps the plant to reproduce.
questions.misconception: Flowers are only for decoration.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes why the stem is important?
options: It is the only green part of the plant
It makes food for the plant
It supports the plant and carries water and food between parts
It absorbs water from the soil
hints: What would happen if the stem were removed?
The stem is like a pipe.
questions.explanation: The stem supports the plant and carries water and food between the roots and the leaves. Without the stem, the plant would fall over and food and water could not move around.
questions.misconception: The stem is only for beauty.

questions.stem: Why do you think the roots are underground and not above the ground?
answer: because roots absorb water from the soil and hold the plant in place underground
because the roots need to take water from the soil
so they can absorb water and hold the plant firmly in the soil
hints: Where is water found?
What holds the plant down?
questions.explanation: Roots are underground because they need to absorb water from the soil and hold the plant firmly in place.
questions.misconception: Roots are above the ground.

questions.stem: Draw a simple plant. Label the root, stem, leaf and flower. Write one function of each part next to its label.

criteria.description: Drew a plant showing all four parts: root, stem, leaf and flower
Wrote a correct function for the root (absorbs water and holds plant)
Wrote a correct function for the stem (supports and carries water/food)
Wrote a correct function for the leaf (makes food using sunlight)
Wrote a correct function for the flower (produces seeds/fruits)

questions.answer: Teacher-assessed using the rubric. Expected drawing: a plant with roots below the soil line, a stem going up, leaves attached to the stem, and a flower at the top.
hints: Think about what you see above and below the ground.
Each part has a special job.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: All parts of a plant do the same work.

questions.stem: A plant's leaves are shaded by a taller tree. What is likely to happen to the plant?
options: It will grow faster because it has shade
It will make less food because it cannot get enough sunlight
It will produce more flowers immediately
The roots will stop absorbing water
hints: What do leaves need to make food?
Without sunlight, can leaves work well?
questions.explanation: Leaves need sunlight to make food. If the leaves are shaded, the plant gets less sunlight and makes less food, so its growth will slow down.
questions.misconception: Leaves can make food without sunlight.

questions.stem: A gardener plants a flower in a pot with very little soil and no room for the roots to spread. What problem will the plant most likely have?
options: It will not be able to absorb enough water
It will produce too many flowers
The leaves will turn to stone
The stem will catch fire
hints: What do roots need to spread and absorb?
Very little soil means less water and minerals.
questions.explanation: Roots need space in the soil to spread and absorb water. With very little soil, the plant cannot absorb enough water and may die or grow poorly.
questions.misconception: Roots can absorb water without soil space.

questions.stem: A farmer notices that one of his maize plants has no flowers. What is the most likely consequence?
options: The plant will grow taller than others
The roots will absorb more water
The plant will not produce seeds or fruits
The stem will change colour
hints: What do flowers produce?
Seeds are needed for the plant to reproduce.
questions.explanation: Flowers produce seeds and fruits. A plant without flowers will not produce seeds or fruits, so it cannot reproduce.
questions.misconception: Flowers are only for decoration.
